ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — RECRUITMENT, SELECTION AND OFFER MANAGEMENT POLICY
Policy ID HR-REC-003 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: Talent Acquisition

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
Defines a fair, consistent, documented hiring process for permanent, fixed-term, internship, and contract roles. Fictional training content; local law and approved employment terms prevail.

2. HEADCOUNT AND ROLE APPROVAL
The hiring manager submits a requisition with business justification, role title, level, location, employment type, reporting manager, job description, budget, headcount approval, and target joining date. Finance and authorized business leadership approve budget before sourcing. Replacement roles identify the vacancy being replaced. Unapproved roles must not be advertised as confirmed vacancies.

3. JOB DESCRIPTION AND ADVERTISING
A job description states responsibilities, essential/desirable skills, experience, location, work arrangement, employment type, and selection stages. Requirements must be job-related and inclusive. Talent Acquisition approves public postings and agency briefs. Internal candidates may apply through internal mobility.

4. SOURCING CHANNELS
Candidates may come from the careers page, employee referrals, campus hiring, professional networks, approved agencies, and permitted job portals. Record the source and avoid duplicate profiles. Referral incentives are governed by the separate referral programme; referral does not guarantee selection.

5. APPLICATION SCREENING
Review relevant experience, skills, qualifications, location, availability, and role requirements. Use consistent criteria for candidates applying to the same role. Do not use unrelated sensitive personal characteristics. Inform candidates if more information is needed.

6. INTERVIEWS
A typical process includes recruiter discussion, technical/functional assessment, hiring-manager interview, and panel or leadership discussion where appropriate. Interviewers use role-related questions and documented scorecards. Submit feedback within 2 working days. Disclose conflicts of interest. Do not ask prohibited or irrelevant personal questions.

7. TECHNICAL AND ROLE ASSESSMENTS
Assessments must be proportionate and time-bounded. Tell candidates the expected duration, criteria, permitted tools, and deadline. Unpaid production work for commercial benefit is prohibited. Store candidate work securely and delete it according to retention rules.

8. BACKGROUND AND REFERENCE CHECKS
Checks are conducted only when relevant, with appropriate notice, consent, and legal basis. They may include employment history, education, professional credentials, and legally permitted identity or criminal checks. Review discrepancies fairly and allow the candidate to explain before an adverse decision. Restrict access to reports.

9. SELECTION AND COMPENSATION
The hiring manager documents selection rationale against role criteria. Compensation must fit the approved range and internal equity principles. Exceptions require HR and designated business approval. Recruiters must not promise unapproved salary, bonus, stock, title, remote work, or joining terms.

10. OFFER APPROVAL AND RELEASE
Before release, approve requisition, selection, compensation, title, location, joining date, and employment type. Use an authorized offer template. Only designated HR representatives may issue or amend formal offers. Verbal discussions do not replace a signed offer.

11. ACCEPTANCE AND PRE-JOINING
Candidate signs and returns the offer by the stated deadline and completes pre-joining tasks. HR coordinates identity and payroll documentation through secure channels. Disclose contingencies such as verification or work authorization where applicable.

12. ONBOARDING HANDOVER
Talent Acquisition hands the case to HR Operations and the hiring manager. Handover includes approved role details, joining date, reporting structure, equipment, access requirements, and agreed accommodations. Manager prepares a first-week plan and assigns a buddy where applicable.

13. CANDIDATE COMMUNICATION
Acknowledge applications, explain next steps, and provide status updates where reasonably possible. Send respectful closure to rejected candidates. Candidate data must not be shared with unauthorized parties.

14. INTERNAL CANDIDATES AND ACCESSIBILITY
Assess internal applicants against the same essential criteria. Do not retaliate against employees exploring internal roles. Candidates may request reasonable interview or assessment accommodations; Talent Acquisition coordinates them confidentially.

15. RECORDS AND RETENTION
Maintain requisition approvals, job descriptions, scorecards, assessment results, offer approvals, and candidate communications. Access is role-based. Retention and deletion follow the Company records schedule and applicable privacy law.

16. EXCEPTIONS AND ESCALATION
Urgent or executive hiring may use an adjusted sequence only with documented HR and business approval. Report suspected discrimination, conflicts of interest, data misuse, or process manipulation to HR leadership or the ethics channel.

ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — EMPLOYEE DOCUMENTATION AND HR RECORDS POLICY
Policy ID HR-OPS-004 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: HR Operations

1. PURPOSE
This guide covers documents collected during recruitment, onboarding, employment, payroll, benefits, and separation. It is fictional training content; actual requirements depend on law, role, and employing entity.

2. PRE-JOINING DOCUMENTS
Depending on the role and legal requirements, HR may request identity/address proof, photograph, education certificates, professional licences, previous employment/relieving letters, signed offer and employment agreement, tax declarations, bank details, emergency contact, and benefit nomination forms. Collect only information needed for a defined purpose.

3. IDENTITY AND ADDRESS VERIFICATION
Submit accepted documents through the official secure HR portal. HR checks name and relevant details and asks the employee to resolve discrepancies. Do not retain original identity documents unless legally required. Never post identity numbers in public channels.

4. EDUCATION AND EMPLOYMENT VERIFICATION
Where relevant, an approved provider may verify degrees, certificates, employment dates, titles, and credentials. Inform the employee and provide a fair opportunity to explain material discrepancies. Reports are confidential and access-controlled.

5. PAYROLL AND TAX RECORDS
Employees provide bank details, tax declarations, and legally required payroll information through the approved payroll system. Update changes promptly. HR/Payroll must restrict access to salary, tax, and bank records. HR will never ask for bank PINs, passwords, or OTPs.

6. STATUTORY AND BENEFIT ENROLLMENT
HR may collect information required for provident fund, employee state insurance, gratuity, professional tax, insurance, nominee, and other statutory/benefit administration. Applicability depends on establishment coverage, wage thresholds, employee category, and current law. Do not assume every scheme applies to every employee.

7. EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT AND POLICY ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
The agreement may specify role, compensation, location, working hours, probation, notice period, confidentiality, intellectual property, and employment conditions. Employees may acknowledge Code of Conduct, information security, acceptable use, privacy, anti-harassment, leave, and expense policies.

8. EMERGENCY CONTACTS AND NOMINEES
Provide an emergency contact and update it when needed. Complete statutory or benefit nominations where required. Use this information only for legitimate emergency or administrative purposes.

9. PERSONAL INFORMATION CHANGES
Notify HR of legal name, address, phone, bank account, tax status, dependant, nominee, or emergency-contact changes. Submit supporting evidence securely. HR verifies and confirms the update.

10. DOCUMENT SECURITY
Use only the HR portal or a verified HR representative. Do not send sensitive documents through public chat, personal email, or unverified links. HR applies role-based access, encryption where available, audit logs, and secure deletion.

11. CORRECTIONS AND EMPLOYEE ACCESS
Raise a ticket identifying the incorrect field and supporting evidence. HR should acknowledge within 3 working days and provide an expected resolution date. Employees must not alter official records or forge, backdate, or falsify documents. Access requests are handled subject to law and security checks.

12. CONFIDENTIALITY AND RETENTION
Employment, identity, payroll, medical, disciplinary, and background-check records have restricted access. Retain records only for legitimate employment, statutory, audit, and dispute-resolution periods under the records schedule.

13. EMPLOYEE SELF-SERVICE
The HR portal may provide payslips, tax statements, leave balances, holiday calendars, policy acknowledgements, personal details, and benefit enrollment. Report missing or incorrect data to HR Operations.

14. SEPARATION DOCUMENTS
At exit, HR coordinates resignation acceptance, notice records, asset return, access removal, final settlement, tax documents, experience/relieving letter where applicable, and benefit closure. Timing and deductions follow applicable law and contract.

15. ESCALATION
For portal access, corrections, payroll records, or verification questions, raise an HR Operations ticket. Report suspected identity theft or unauthorized disclosure immediately through the security incident channel.

ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — LEAVE AND TIME-OFF POLICY
Policy ID HR-LEAVE-001 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: Human Resources | Scope: India-based employees, subject to applicable law and contract.

IMPORTANT: This is fictional training content. Entitlements and figures are illustrative company benefits, not legal advice. Applicable Indian central/state laws, establishment rules, and employment contracts prevail wherever they provide a greater or different entitlement.

1. LEAVE YEAR AND ADMINISTRATION
The leave year is 1 January–31 December. Leave is recorded in the HR portal. Employees should check balances before applying. Apply with dates, leave category, and handover details. Managers should normally respond to planned requests within 3 working days. Silence is not approval. Notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible for emergencies. Medical and family documents must be submitted only through confidential HR channels.

2. CASUAL LEAVE (CL)
Illustrative entitlement: 12 working days per calendar year, credited monthly. Use for personal work, urgent family needs, or short absences. Request at least one working day ahead where practical. For emergencies, notify the manager and submit the portal request later. Casual leave is not normally carried forward or encashed.

3. EARNED / PRIVILEGE LEAVE (EL/PL)
Illustrative entitlement: 18 working days per year, accrued at 1.5 days per completed month. Use for planned vacations and extended personal commitments. Requests of 3 or more consecutive working days should normally be submitted 10 calendar days in advance. Sample carry-forward ceiling: 30 days. Encashment and separation treatment follow applicable law and contract.

4. SICK LEAVE (SL)
Illustrative entitlement: 12 working days per year. Use for illness, injury, medical appointments, treatment, and recovery. Inform the manager before the shift where possible. A medical certificate may be requested for an absence exceeding 2 consecutive working days, subject to applicable law and consistent administration. Medical records remain confidential.

5. MATERNITY LEAVE
Eligible employees receive maternity leave and protections under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended, and other applicable law. As a general statutory reference, eligible women with fewer than two surviving children may receive up to 26 weeks, with no more than 8 weeks before the expected delivery date; for two or more surviving children, the general entitlement is up to 12 weeks, with no more than 6 weeks before delivery. Eligibility, establishment coverage, adoption/commissioning provisions, and individual circumstances must be checked against current law. Contact HR as early as practical. Submit statutory notice and required documents confidentially. Nursing breaks, work-from-home possibilities where the role permits, and crèche obligations are handled as required by applicable law. Maternity leave is not deducted from ordinary casual or earned leave.

6. PATERNITY / PARTNER LEAVE
Illustrative Company benefit: 10 paid working days after the birth of a child, to be used within 90 days of birth. It may be taken continuously or in two blocks with HR/manager approval. Provide reasonable notice and proof of birth through the confidential HR channel. This is a sample private-company benefit, not a general statutory paternity entitlement for all private-sector employees in India.

7. ADOPTION AND COMMISSIONING PARENT LEAVE
Statutory leave for adopting and commissioning mothers is governed by applicable law, including the Maternity Benefit Act where applicable. The Company also provides an illustrative 10 working days of paid bonding leave to an eligible non-birth parent after placement or birth. Contact HR before the expected placement date. Submit only the documents needed to verify eligibility.

8. BEREAVEMENT LEAVE
Illustrative benefit: up to 5 paid working days after the death of a spouse, child, parent, sibling, or a person for whom the employee was primary caregiver; up to 2 days for a grandparent, parent-in-law, or other close relative. HR may approve additional earned or unpaid leave for travel or exceptional circumstances.

9. MARRIAGE LEAVE
Illustrative benefit: 3 paid working days for an employee's own marriage, once during employment. Request 15 days in advance where practical. This is separate from earned leave.

10. COMPENSATORY OFF
Work on a weekly off or declared holiday qualifies only when approved in advance by the manager and recorded in the HR portal. Use approved comp-off within 60 days, subject to operational needs and applicable law. Staying late on a normal workday does not automatically create comp-off.

11. UNPAID LEAVE / LEAVE WITHOUT PAY
When paid balances are exhausted, employees may request unpaid leave. Approval is discretionary except where law protects the absence. Payroll deductions follow applicable rules. Unapproved absence may be reviewed under the disciplinary process.

12. PUBLIC HOLIDAYS AND OPTIONAL HOLIDAYS
The Company publishes a location-specific annual holiday calendar. Employees may select up to 2 optional holidays from the published list with manager approval. Weekly offs and holidays during leave are treated according to applicable law, location rules, and HR system configuration.

13. PROBATION, NOTICE PERIOD AND SEPARATION
Leave accrual begins on joining unless the contract says otherwise. Planned leave during probation or notice period requires approval, but statutory rights remain unaffected. Unused balances at separation are settled according to applicable law and contract.

14. EXTENSION, CANCELLATION AND ESCALATION
Request extensions before the approved end date. In emergencies, notify the manager as soon as possible. Raise balance errors, inconsistent decisions, or eligibility questions with HR Operations. If this policy conflicts with law, law prevails.

15. QUICK REFERENCE — ILLUSTRATIVE COMPANY BENEFITS
Casual: 12 days/year | Earned: 18 days/year | Sick: 12 days/year
Partner/paternity: 10 working days | Marriage: 3 working days
Bereavement: up to 5 working days for immediate family
Earned leave carry-forward sample cap: 30 days
Verify maternity, adoption, holiday, and all statutory entitlements with HR and current law.

ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — MEDICAL INSURANCE, HEALTH BENEFITS AND WELLNESS POLICY
Policy ID HR-MED-002 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: Benefits Team | Scope: Eligible India-based employees.

IMPORTANT: Fictional RAG training content. Actual coverage is determined only by the insurer's policy wording, schedule, endorsements, network list, and applicable law. Sample limits below are not guaranteed benefits or medical advice.

1. ELIGIBILITY AND ENROLLMENT
Regular full-time employees are eligible subject to insurer enrollment rules. Interns, consultants, temporary employees, and dependants are covered only if expressly included. HR shares enrollment instructions after joining. Confirm the effective date on the insurer e-card before assuming coverage has started.

2. DEPENDANTS
The illustrative base plan covers the employee, legally married spouse, and up to two dependent children. Optional parent/parent-in-law coverage may be offered at additional premium. Age limits, dependency proof, family definitions, and enrollment windows are controlled by the insurer. Report marriage, birth, adoption, or dependant changes within 30 days.

3. SUM INSURED AND TOP-UP
Illustrative base group cover: INR 5,00,000 per family per policy year, shared among covered members. Optional top-up bands may be INR 5,00,000 or INR 10,00,000. Deductibles, co-payments, room-rent limits, sub-limits, and waiting periods are insurer-specific. These amounts are invented sample values.

4. INPATIENT HOSPITALIZATION
Subject to the policy, cover may include medically necessary hospitalization, room and nursing charges within limits, surgeon/consultant fees, operation theatre, prescribed medicines, diagnostics, and eligible treatment. Minimum hospitalization periods and room-category restrictions may apply. Confirm network status and pre-authorization for planned admission.

5. DAY-CARE PROCEDURES
Listed procedures not requiring 24-hour admission may be covered, such as dialysis, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, cataract surgery, and specified endoscopic procedures. Only procedures listed by the insurer and meeting medical-necessity rules qualify.

6. PRE- AND POST-HOSPITALIZATION
Illustrative sample: eligible expenses up to 30 days before and 60 days after an approved hospitalization, when related to the same illness/injury and permitted by the plan. Submit prescriptions, test reports, bills, and discharge summary. Verify actual time limits in the policy schedule.

7. MATERNITY AND NEWBORN COVER
If included, maternity cover may reimburse eligible delivery and pregnancy-related hospitalization subject to sub-limits, waiting periods, number-of-child conditions, and exclusions. Illustrative limits: INR 75,000 normal delivery and INR 1,00,000 caesarean delivery. Newborn cover may start at birth or another date specified by the insurer. Notify HR promptly after birth to add the child. Maternity insurance is separate from statutory maternity leave.

8. OUTPATIENT, DENTAL AND VISION
Routine OPD, dental, and vision costs are not automatically covered by the sample base plan. A separate rider may reimburse up to INR 5,000 per employee per year for eligible consultations, prescribed medicines, basic dental treatment, or eye examination. Cosmetic procedures and non-prescribed products are excluded unless explicitly included.

9. MENTAL HEALTH AND COUNSELLING
The sample Employee Assistance Programme provides up to 6 confidential counselling sessions per year, subject to provider availability. EAP sessions are separate from insurance claims. Psychiatric consultations, therapy, and hospitalization are covered only as stated in the insurance policy and applicable law. Managers do not receive counselling details. For emergencies, contact local emergency services or a qualified provider.

10. PREVENTIVE CARE AND WELLNESS
The Company may arrange one annual preventive check-up for eligible employees aged 25 and above, subject to vendor and plan terms. Wellness initiatives may include vaccination information, ergonomics, fitness, nutrition, and stress-management sessions. Participation is voluntary unless a lawful role-specific occupational check is required.

11. CASHLESS HOSPITALIZATION
For planned admission, use a network hospital and ask its insurance desk to submit pre-authorization before admission. Carry e-card and identity proof. Cashless approval is not final claim settlement; the insurer may reassess after discharge. In emergencies, seek care first and notify insurer/TPA as soon as practical within its stated deadline.

12. REIMBURSEMENT CLAIMS
Where reimbursement is permitted, submit the claim form, e-card, discharge summary, itemized final bill, payment receipts, prescriptions, investigation reports, pharmacy bills, and required bank details through the official secure portal. Submit within the insurer deadline. Keep originals until settlement. Never send records to unverified email addresses.

13. CLAIM QUERIES, REJECTION AND APPEAL
The insurer/TPA evaluates medical necessity, coverage, exclusions, waiting periods, sub-limits, and documentation. Respond to queries through the official portal. If rejected, request written reasons and the relevant policy clause, then use the insurer grievance process and applicable regulator escalation route. HR can help locate documents but cannot guarantee approval.

14. EXCLUSIONS AND LIMITATIONS
Depending on wording, exclusions may include non-medical consumables, cosmetic treatment, non-prescribed supplements, routine OPD without rider, excluded providers, costs above sub-limits, applicable waiting periods, and non-medically necessary treatment. The actual policy wording controls.

15. PRE-EXISTING CONDITIONS AND DISCLOSURE
Waiting periods and disclosure requirements vary. Answer insurer enrollment questions accurately. Ask the insurer/TPA for written clarification before planned treatment. HR should not collect unnecessary diagnosis details.

16. WORKPLACE ACCOMMODATION
Employees needing temporary or ongoing adjustments should contact HR. The Company considers reasonable adjustments based on role, safety, medical recommendations, and applicable law. Managers generally need functional restrictions and expected duration, not detailed clinical records.

17. PRIVACY AND SECURITY
Medical records and claim data are sensitive. Insurer, TPA, and authorized Benefits personnel may process information for enrollment and claims. Access is restricted. Use approved confidential channels and never share another employee's e-card.

18. EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITIES AND CONTACTS
Keep e-card accessible, update dependants, verify network hospitals, obtain pre-authorization, submit complete claims on time, retain receipts, and protect medical information. Contact Benefits Operations for enrollment and policy copies; contact insurer/TPA for claim status.

ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — INCIDENT MANAGEMENT AND ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS STANDARD
Policy ID ENG-RCA-005 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: Engineering Operations

1. PURPOSE
Defines detection, severity, response, communication, recovery, post-incident review, and corrective action tracking. Fictional technical training content.

2. DEFINITIONS
Incident: unplanned interruption or degradation.
Major incident: significant customer, security, financial, regulatory, or operational impact.
Root cause: underlying condition that made the incident possible.
Contributing factor: condition increasing likelihood, duration, or impact.
Mitigation: action reducing impact without necessarily removing root cause.

3. SEVERITY
SEV-1 Critical: broad outage, major data integrity issue, active compromise, or severe business impact. Immediate incident command and executive notification.
SEV-2 High: significant degradation of important service or customer group, limited workaround.
SEV-3 Medium: limited impact or viable workaround.
SEV-4 Low: minor defect or informational event.
Incident commander may change severity and must record rationale.

4. DETECTION AND DECLARATION
Sources include monitoring, customer reports, service desk, security tools, and employee observations. Record time, service, symptoms, and evidence. Notify on-call engineer and incident commander immediately for suspected SEV-1/SEV-2.

5. ROLES
Incident Commander coordinates priorities and response.
Technical Lead directs diagnosis and remediation.
Communications Lead sends approved updates.
Scribe records timeline and decisions.
Service Owner validates recovery and follow-up.
Responsibilities must be explicit, even when one person holds multiple roles.

6. RESPONSE WORKFLOW
Acknowledge alert; declare severity; open incident channel and record; assess scope and impact; stabilize; choose mitigation; communicate; verify recovery; monitor; close operational incident; schedule review. Preserve evidence without exposing secrets or unnecessary personal data.

7. COMMUNICATION
For SEV-1, internal updates at least every 30 minutes; SEV-2 at least hourly while impact continues. State known impact, actions, workaround, and next update time. Do not speculate or assign blame. Customer communications follow the approved plan.

8. RCA REQUIRED SECTIONS
Incident ID/title; date; severity; service owner/authors; executive summary; customer impact; start/detection/mitigation/resolution times; timeline; technical root cause; contributing factors; detection gaps; what went well; what failed; remediation; lessons learned; action owners and due dates. Separate confirmed facts from hypotheses.

9. BLAMELESS REVIEW
Focus on system conditions, design, safeguards, monitoring, documentation, and process. Do not attribute failure to personal character or intent. Misconduct and security investigations follow separate confidential processes.

10. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
Every action needs description, priority, accountable owner, due date, tracking ticket, and measurable completion criteria. Valid actions include tests, code fixes, capacity changes, alerts, runbook updates, access changes, training, or architecture work. "Be more careful" is not an acceptable action.

11. REVIEW DEADLINES
Review SEV-1/SEV-2 incidents normally within 5 working days and useful SEV-3 reviews within 10 working days. Publish approved RCA after security/privacy review. Track overdue actions in engineering reviews.

12. SECURITY AND DATA INCIDENTS
Report suspected exposure, credential compromise, malware, or unauthorized access immediately through Security process. Do not delete logs, independently notify external parties, or investigate beyond authority. Legal/privacy teams decide regulatory notifications.

13. EXAMPLE
A reporting API returns HTTP 503 for 18 minutes after deployment changes connection-pool limit. Rollback restores service. Root cause includes missing load test and absent saturation alert. Actions: add load test, alert, deployment checklist, owners, and due dates.

14. RECOVERY AND METRICS
Service owner verifies health checks, error rates, latency, queue depth, and customer functionality. Track time to acknowledge, time to mitigate, recurrence, change-related incidents, action completion, and alert quality. Use metrics to improve systems, not rank individuals without context.

ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — IT OPERATIONS AND INFORMATION SECURITY POLICY
Policy ID IT-SEC-006 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: IT and Information Security

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This policy covers accounts, access, devices, data handling, email, remote work, software development, incidents, backups, vendors, and production changes. Fictional RAG training content.

2. IDENTITY AND ACCESS
Use assigned corporate identity and SSO. MFA is mandatory on supported systems. Shared accounts are prohibited unless formally approved and controlled. Never share passwords, recovery codes, API keys, session cookies, or OTPs.

3. ACCESS REQUESTS
Submit application, business justification, requested role, duration, data classification, and manager approval through the service desk. System owners approve least-privilege access. Privileged access needs additional approval and stronger authentication. Temporary access must expire automatically.

4. JOINER, MOVER, LEAVER
HR triggers onboarding and separation workflows. IT provisions approved access, adjusts permissions on role changes, and promptly disables accounts at separation or authorized instruction. Managers must report transfers and departures. Rotate exposed secrets immediately.

5. PASSWORDS AND MFA
Use unique passwords and an approved password manager. Do not reuse corporate passwords on personal sites. Reject unexpected MFA prompts. Report repeated prompts, phishing, or account lockouts. IT will never ask for passwords or OTPs in chat.

6. DEVICE SECURITY
Company devices must use supported operating systems, screen locks, disk encryption, endpoint protection, and security updates. Do not disable controls or install unapproved software. Report lost/stolen devices immediately for session revocation or authorized remote wipe.

7. DATA CLASSIFICATION
Public: approved for public release.
Internal: routine information for employees and approved partners.
Confidential: business plans, non-public financial data, customer contracts, operational information.
Restricted: credentials, personal data, payment data, security secrets, and regulated information.
Apply suitable access, encryption, sharing, retention, and deletion controls.

8. STORAGE AND SHARING
Use approved Company storage. Share only with intended recipients and minimum permissions. Public links for Confidential/Restricted data are prohibited unless a documented exception is approved. Verify recipients. Do not upload Company data to personal cloud or unapproved AI services.

9. EMAIL AND PHISHING
Be cautious with unexpected attachments, login links, payment instructions, and credential requests. Verify unusual requests using a separate trusted channel. Report suspicious messages using the mail client or Security service desk. Do not forward malicious files to colleagues.

10. NETWORK AND REMOTE WORK
Use approved VPN or zero-trust access where required. Avoid untrusted public Wi-Fi for sensitive work unless approved protection is active. Secure devices physically and do not let others use corporate devices. Report suspected compromise.

11. SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT AND SECRETS
Use approved repositories. Never commit secrets, keys, tokens, or production data. Use a secrets manager and scoped service identities. Review dependencies, scan code, and restrict production access. Security testing must stay within authorized scope.

12. CHANGE AND RELEASE MANAGEMENT
Production changes require an approved change record, risk assessment, testing evidence, deployment/monitoring plan, and rollback procedure. Emergency changes may use expedited approval but must be documented and reviewed afterward. Unapproved direct production changes are prohibited.

13. INCIDENT REPORTING
Immediately report phishing, malware, lost devices, exposed credentials, unauthorized access, data leakage, or unusual activity through the official Security channel. Include time, system, symptoms, and safe evidence. Do not destroy logs or investigate beyond authority.

14. SERVICE DESK PRIORITY
P1: critical outage or active broad-impact security incident.
P2: major degradation or important function unavailable.
P3: limited impact with workaround.
P4: general question or low-priority request.
Security incidents may be escalated independently of normal priority.

15. BACKUP AND RECOVERY
System owners define backup frequency, retention, encryption, RPO, and RTO. Restrict backup access and test restoration periodically. A successful backup job alone does not prove recoverability.

16. THIRD-PARTY ACCESS
Vendor access needs a business owner, contract/approval, least privilege, expiry, and monitoring. Disable access when work ends or the agreement expires.

17. ACCEPTABLE USE AND EXCEPTIONS
Limited personal use may be allowed if lawful, secure, and non-disruptive. Harassment, unlawful content, piracy, bypassing controls, fraud, and unauthorized monitoring are prohibited. Exceptions require documented justification, risk acceptance, compensating controls, and expiry date. Violations may result in access suspension or disciplinary review.

ZORVEX TECHNOLOGIES — BUSINESS TRAVEL AND EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
Policy ID FIN-TRV-007 | Version 2.0 | Effective 1 November 2026
Owner: Finance Operations

1. PURPOSE
Covers travel approval, booking, accommodation, meals, transport, claims, reimbursement, advances, exceptions, and audit. Fictional RAG training content; all sample limits must be replaced by actual approved limits.

2. PRE-TRAVEL APPROVAL
Obtain written manager approval before booking. Request must state business purpose, destination, dates, attendees, estimated cost, project/cost centre, and expected outcome. International travel may require business-head, Finance, Legal, or security approval. Personal extensions must be separated from Company costs.

3. BOOKING PRINCIPLES
Use approved portal/agency where available. Choose safe, reasonable, cost-effective options. Compare total cost, cancellation terms, travel time, and baggage. Do not split bookings to avoid approval thresholds.

4. AIR AND RAIL
Sample default is economy class for domestic and international flights. Premium economy/business class requires documented exception approval for journey duration, medical accommodation, or business necessity. Rail class must be appropriate to duration and safety. Personal upgrades are not reimbursed unless approved.

5. HOTEL
Illustrative domestic hotel ceiling: INR 6,000/night before taxes. Higher cost requires prior written approval. Choose safe accommodation near work location. Minibar, entertainment, spa, guest charges, and personal upgrades are excluded unless approved.

6. MEALS AND INCIDENTALS
Illustrative meal ceiling: INR 1,200 per travel day. Alcohol, personal shopping, tobacco, and non-business guest meals are excluded. Client meals require attendee names, business purpose, itemized receipt, and manager approval. Tips must be reasonable.

7. LOCAL TRANSPORT
Reasonable taxi, rideshare, public transit, airport transfer, and parking may be reimbursed for approved business travel. Personal commuting, traffic fines, and avoidable premium transport are excluded. Obtain receipts where available.

8. PERSONAL VEHICLE
Prior manager approval is required. Employee must hold valid licence and insurance. Illustrative mileage rate: INR 10/km, subject to Finance confirmation. Record date, route, purpose, and distance. Tolls and parking may be claimed separately with receipts.

9. CLAIM SUBMISSION
Submit through expense portal within 15 calendar days after trip end. Each line needs date, merchant, category, amount, currency, business purpose, cost centre, and required receipt. Use approved exchange-rate method. Duplicate claims are prohibited.

10. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS
Attach itemized invoices, payment proof, booking confirmation, boarding pass where applicable, approval record, and attendee details for business meals. Explain missing receipts and provide alternative evidence. Finance may reject unsupported or illegible claims.

11. REVIEW AND REIMBURSEMENT
Finance checks approvals, policy compliance, arithmetic, receipt quality, duplicates, tax treatment, and cost centre. Incomplete claims may be returned. Approved claims are normally paid in the next scheduled cycle, subject to payroll cut-off and bank processing.

12. ADVANCES AND COMPANY CARDS
Advances require approval and reconciliation within 15 calendar days after return. Company cards are for approved business costs only. Upload receipts and explain unusual transactions. Report lost cards immediately to issuer and Finance.

13. CANCELLATIONS AND CHANGES
Cancel unused bookings promptly. Company-funded refunds and credits belong to the Company. Do not retain travel credits for personal use. Business-related change fees may be reimbursed with approval.

14. NON-REIMBURSABLE COSTS
Personal entertainment/shopping, traffic fines, penalties, tobacco, alcohol unless specifically approved for a permitted business event, companion travel, avoidable no-show fees, and non-business costs are excluded.

15. EXCEPTIONS AND EMERGENCIES
Get written approval before exceeding limits where practical. If emergency prevents prior approval, notify manager and Finance promptly and submit explanation/evidence. Finance records exception decision.

16. FRAUD AND AUDIT
Falsified receipts, duplicate claims, personal expenses presented as business, or misuse of advances may trigger investigation and disciplinary action. Finance may audit claims and request original evidence.

17. TAX AND COMPLIANCE
Provide accurate information for tax/statutory reporting. Finance determines tax treatment under applicable law. Reimbursement is not automatically tax-free.

18. QUICK REFERENCE — FICTIONAL SAMPLE LIMITS
Hotel: INR 6,000/night | Meals: INR 1,200/day | Personal vehicle: INR 10/km
Claim deadline: 15 calendar days after trip completion.
